name: Chedorlaomer
source_summary: King of Elam who led a coalition of four eastern kings against five Canaanite kings, defeating them and carrying off Lot as a captive, until Abram pursued and routed his forces to rescue Lot.
family_friendly_summary: Chedorlaomer was a powerful king from Elam, far to the east. For twelve years he ruled over several smaller kings near the Dead Sea, including the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah. When those kings rebelled against him, Chedorlaomer gathered three other kings and marched west to fight them. His army won the battle, and as they left, they carried off people and goods from Sodom -- including Abram's nephew Lot, who lived there. When Abram heard Lot had been taken, he gathered his own men, chased Chedorlaomer's army by night, defeated them, and brought Lot and everyone else safely home.
adult_story: Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, held five Canaanite kings -- including the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah -- under tribute for twelve years (Genesis 14:1-4). When they rebelled in the thirteenth year, Chedorlaomer marched west the following year with three allied kings, first crushing several other peoples (the Rephaim, Zuzim, Emim, and Horites) before routing the five rebel kings in the tar-pit-filled Valley of Siddim (14:5-10). The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fell into the pits while fleeing, and the victors plundered Sodom and Gomorrah, carrying off goods, food, and captives -- including Lot, Abram's nephew, who was living in Sodom (14:11-12). When a survivor reported this to Abram, he armed 318 of his own trained men, pursued Chedorlaomer's retreating forces by night as far north as Dan, routed them, and pursued them further to Hobah, recovering Lot, the other captives, and all the plundered goods (14:13-16). Returning victorious, Abram was met and blessed by Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, to whom Abram gave a tenth of everything (14:17-20). Chedorlaomer himself speaks no words and receives no further mention in Scripture -- his campaign exists in the text chiefly as the occasion for Abram's decisive rescue of Lot and his first recorded encounter with Melchizedek.

devotionals: Abram's daring rescue of Lot from Chedorlaomer's army pictures a far greater rescue -- Jesus, who frees us from sin and death.
After defeating Chedorlaomer, Abram was blessed by Melchizedek, a priest and king, with bread and wine. That points forward to Jesus, our own priest and king.
